questions.question: Day 11 Practice (Morning & Home Routines (Phase 2)): When talking about withdrawing cash from ATM (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My manager'?

options.a: Card cash withdrawal taking? yesterday
options.b: Is this card accepted at the cash withdrawal counter?
options.c: I am withdrawing cash from ATM right now.
options.d: Card cash withdrawal taking?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Is this card accepted at the cash withdrawal counter?".

questions.question: Day 11 Vocabulary (Morning & Home Routines (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'freshen up'?

options.a: Wash hands and face to relax after travel.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'freshen up' means: wash hands and face to relax after travel. Example: "Let me freshen up after returning home."

questions.question:
Day 11 Translation Scenario 1 (Morning & Home Routines (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నా పార్సెల్ ఈ రోజు సాయంత్రానికి డెలివరీ అవుతుందా?"
(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Will my package be delivered by this evening?
options.c: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.d: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.

questions.question:
Day 11 Translation Scenario 2 (Morning & Home Routines (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.
options.d: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.
